**Triage: lands in `packages/cli/src/utils/format.ts` (the boot banner) and the first-run seed path; `domain:cli`; `priority:p2`.**

⭐ **This card has something most do not: a named real user and their words.** The maintainer of a downstream app (`objectstack-ai/ats`) ran `pnpm dev`, signed in with **the credential the terminal handed them**, opened the app, and got an empty left navigation — 「我刚管理员登录进去,看不到 ATS 的左侧菜单」.

⇒ **The app was working correctly. The account was the problem, and the platform is what pointed them at it.** The boot banner's `🔑 Dev admin` is the **only** credential a first-run operator is given, and in any audience-gated app it is the account that sees nothing.

⇒ p2: this is a first-run experience defect that makes a working product look broken, and the person best placed to misdiagnose it is the one we handed the credential to.

⇒ ⚠️ **Two exits, and the implementer must pick deliberately and say which:**
- make the offered credential actually usable in an audience-gated app, **or**
- keep it and make the banner **say what this account will and will not see**, naming how to reach a scoped account.

⛔ Silence is not an option — that is the current state. ⚠️ **If the fix means changing what the first-run seed creates**, that is a product-shape change ⇒ **stop and report** rather than deciding it in a PR.

`Size/model suggestion:` M.

`Contract-text:` — the published statement this card is measured against, `AGENTS.md:133` at `edaf3b2f`:

> `admin@objectos.ai` / `admin123`, override via `--admin-email`/`--admin-password`). The seeded admin is auto-promoted to …

⇒ the credential and its promotion are documented; ⛔ nothing here removes or renames either. Banner **copy** is not a contract surface, no key is added to any published payload, and no symbol is exported ⇒ `no`. ⚠️ **Provisional and re-graded from the delivered diff**: it flips to `yes` if the branch adds a key to a published schema — which is precisely what suggestion 1 (`devHint` / `devLogins[]`) would do, and that is the boundary below.

### Prior-ruling search — run BEFORE this claim, and it found the governing precedent

⭐ **ADR-0115 `:93`** rules on this exact class, one level up. It records that a guard which was 「complete in its refusal and **silent in its permission**」 reproduced the same defect it existed to close, because 「the operator's only evidence of a degraded state is the env var they may not have set themselves」. The remedy it adopted is triage's second exit almost word for word — **brand the condition where the operator looks** — with two cited precedents: `OS_ALLOW_DEGRADED_TENANCY` 「boots degraded *and brands it everywhere an operator looks*」, and `resolveAllowDriverConnectFailure`'s contract, 「logged loudly at startup」.

⚠️ **And the same paragraph cuts the other way, which is why it must be read and not just cited.** It says the dev-admin seed was **deliberately excluded** from that warning set: 「`plugin-auth`'s `maybeSeedDevAdmin` is hard-gated to `NODE_ENV === 'development'` and cannot fire on this path, and **a warning about a non-event spends the attention the real ones need**」.

⇒ That exclusion was reasoned about a **production-hazard** warning, and this card argues a different harm — an *audience-gated* app where the named account sees nothing. Those are compatible, but the compatibility has to be **argued from the ADR's own text**, ⛔ not assumed by whoever implements this. If the honest reading is that ADR-0115 already settled it against branding, that is a report, ⛔ not a PR.

Controls: 65 `docs/adr/*` files match `permission`; 38 `describe(` in `packages/spec/src/kernel/manifest.zod.ts`; a fabricated term returns 0.

### The boundary this card must not cross on its own

Triage: 「⚠️ **If the fix means changing what the first-run seed creates**, that is a product-shape change ⇒ **stop and report** rather than deciding it in a PR.」

⚠️ I am adding one more of the same kind, from this lane's red line (「按落点判归属」): **suggestion 1 as written needs a new key on a published schema in `packages/spec`** — a different seat's lane, and 「已发布载荷上的新键恒 `yes`」 under the mechanical floor. ⇒ if the deliberate choice lands there, it is a **stop-and-report**, ⛔ not a cross-lane edit. Suggestion 3 the card itself flags as possibly `objectui` ⇒ likewise out of scope here.

⇒ What is dispatchable **within this lane** is the banner's own words. Triage's 「⛔ Silence is not an option — that is the current state」 still binds, and the exit choice is the implementer's to make deliberately and to state.

## Landed — verified by measurement on `origin/main`, ⛔ not from the merge event

**Commit:** `f721ef0ff2880dd3fc5389d5d4585b825252122e` — 「fix(cli): the boot banner's `🔑 Dev admin` says what that account will and will not see (#17555)」, 2026-09-10T22:50:42Z.

**Shape:** `git rev-list --parents -n 1 f721ef0f` ⇒ **2 fields = single parent = squash.**

**Content present, controlled:** `requiredPermissions` ⇒ **4** in `packages/cli/src/utils/format.ts`; the new pin `format.server-ready-dev-admin-audience.test.ts` is in the tree. A fabricated symbol over `packages/cli/src` returns **0**.

**Card disposition:** closed `completed` at 23:12:01Z by the PR's own `Closes #17081`. `pm:dispatched` stripped with a targeted `DELETE`.

### What shipped

Triage's **second** exit, taken deliberately: the seeded credential is unchanged, and the banner now says what that account reaches, the mechanism that hides an app from it — it holds **no** app-declared capability, so an app gating navigation on `requiredPermissions` may show it an empty menu — and two routes to a scoped account. Exit 1 was refused with a stated reason: it is reachable only by changing what the first-run seed creates, which triage rules a product-shape stop-and-report, and the platform cannot know an app's audience in any case.

⭐ **The central claim is measured, not asserted.** On a live `pnpm dev --fresh` boot, signed in as the printed credential, `GET /api/v1/auth/me/permissions` returned **8 capabilities, all platform built-ins, ZERO app-declared** — and a scoped persona served as the positive control proving the `requiredPermissions` filter was live on that boot rather than failing open. The routes the new text points at were verified to exist rather than assumed, which is the failure mode ADR-0115's amendment is about.

### The two halves this card carried, filed before it closed

⚠️ `Closes #17081` would have taken them with it — a local grep over all **91** open `domain:cli` + `repo:objectui` cards found `devHint`, `devLogins` and `empty shell` in **this card alone** (positive control `plugin` 30/91; fabricated term 0).

- **#17556** — let an app contribute its own first-run credentials (`devHint` / `devLogins[]`), routed `domain:spec`, because a new key on a published schema is always clause-② `yes` under the mechanical floor. This is the half this card itself called 「the fix that scales — the app is the only party that knows what its audiences are」.
- **#17557** — the objectui half: say so when navigation resolves to zero entries instead of rendering an empty shell.

⭐ And recorded for whoever picks those up: the in-repo showcase app declares no `requiredPermissions` of its own, so it **cannot** reproduce the empty-navigation shape this card reports downstream. ⛔ A full showcase nav is not evidence against this card.
